tonic.name: Tonic
tonic.meaning: Home and resolution; iii and vi can prolong tonic, depending on context.

predominant.name: Predominant
predominant.meaning: Motion away from home, often preparing the dominant. Also called the subdominant family.

dominant.name: Dominant
dominant.meaning: Tension and a tendency to resolve to tonic.

context.name: Context dependent
context.meaning: Its role depends on the surrounding progression.

contextNote: These are useful tonal-harmony families, not fixed rules. The mediant (iii / III) is especially context dependent and can also participate in dominant motion.
minorNote: Minor keys mix forms: natural minor has v and VII (subtonic). Raising degree 7 gives V and vii° with stronger pull to i. Harmonic minor also changes III to III+; not every minor-key chord must come from one fixed scale.
